question: Within 1000 metres of Avenida das Tulipas, for each building subtype return the tallest building, with its height in metres and its distance to the nearest segment of that road in metres; break ties by building id and return the top-ranked building per subtype.
sql: WITH road AS (SELECT ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_roads WHERE names."primary" = 'Avenida das Tulipas'), building_dist AS (SELECT b.id, b.subtype, b.names."primary" AS building_name, b.height, MIN(ST_Distance(ST_Transform(b.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true), r.geom_3763)) AS distance_m FROM lisbon_buildings b CROSS JOIN road r GROUP BY b.id, b.subtype, b.names."primary", b.height HAVING MIN(ST_Distance(ST_Transform(b.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true), r.geom_3763)) <= 1000), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subtype ORDER BY height DESC, id) AS rn FROM building_dist) SELECT subtype, building_name, height, distance_m FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY subtype;

question: For each road class, list the three longest road segments by length in metres, and include the cumulative length in metres of those top-ranked segments within the class when ordered by length descending; break ties by road id.
sql: WITH road_lengths AS (SELECT id, class, names."primary" AS road_name, ST_Length(ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true)) AS length_m FROM lisbon_roads), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY class ORDER BY length_m DESC, id) AS rn FROM road_lengths), top3 AS (SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3) SELECT class, road_name, length_m, SUM(length_m) OVER (PARTITION BY class ORDER BY length_m DESC, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_top_length_m FROM top3 ORDER BY class, rn;

question: For each roof shape, identify the largest building footprint in square metres that lies within 200 metres of at least one road segment classified as footway; return the roof shape, building name, footprint area in square metres, and distance to the nearest such footway in metres; break ties by building id.
sql: WITH buildings AS (SELECT id, roof_shape, names."primary" AS building_name, ST_Area(ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true)) AS area_m2, ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_buildings), footways AS (SELECT ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_roads WHERE class = 'footway'), building_dist AS (SELECT b.id, b.roof_shape, b.building_name, b.area_m2, MIN(ST_Distance(b.geom_3763, f.geom_3763)) AS distance_m FROM buildings b CROSS JOIN footways f GROUP BY b.id, b.roof_shape, b.building_name, b.area_m2 HAVING MIN(ST_Distance(b.geom_3763, f.geom_3763)) <= 200), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY roof_shape ORDER BY area_m2 DESC, id) AS rn FROM building_dist) SELECT roof_shape, building_name, area_m2, distance_m FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY roof_shape;

question: For each road class, identify the two road segments closest to any building of subtype 'civic', returning the road class, road name, distance in metres to the nearest civic building, and the rank within the class by ascending distance; only consider road segments within 500 metres of a civic building.
sql: WITH civic_buildings AS (SELECT ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_buildings WHERE subtype = 'civic'), roads AS (SELECT id, class, names."primary" AS road_name, ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_roads), road_dist AS (SELECT r.id, r.class, r.road_name, MIN(ST_Distance(r.geom_3763, c.geom_3763)) AS distance_m FROM roads r CROSS JOIN civic_buildings c GROUP BY r.id, r.class, r.road_name HAVING MIN(ST_Distance(r.geom_3763, c.geom_3763)) <= 500), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY class ORDER BY distance_m ASC, id) AS rn FROM road_dist) SELECT class, road_name, distance_m, rn FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 2 ORDER BY class, rn;

question: For residential buildings within 500 metres of Rua de Campolide, order them by distance to that road ascending and compute the running total of their heights in metres; return the 10 closest buildings with their height and the running height total.
sql: WITH road AS (SELECT ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_roads WHERE names."primary" = 'Rua de Campolide'), building_dist AS (SELECT b.id, b.names."primary" AS building_name, b.height, MIN(ST_Distance(ST_Transform(b.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true), r.geom_3763)) AS distance_m FROM lisbon_buildings b CROSS JOIN road r WHERE b.subtype = 'residential' GROUP BY b.id, b.names."primary", b.height HAVING MIN(ST_Distance(ST_Transform(b.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true), r.geom_3763)) <= 500) SELECT building_name, height, distance_m, SUM(height) OVER (ORDER BY distance_m ASC, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_height_m FROM building_dist ORDER BY distance_m ASC, id LIMIT 10;

question: Within 1 kilometre of the point (-9.1472, 38.7078), for each building subtype rank buildings by height descending and compute the running total of heights in metres for the top three buildings per subtype; return the subtype, building name, height, and running total.
sql: WITH point AS (SELECT ST_Transform(ST_Point(-9.1472, 38.7078), 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763), buildings AS (SELECT b.id, b.subtype, b.names."primary" AS building_name, b.height, ST_Transform(b.geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3763', always_xy := true) AS geom_3763 FROM lisbon_buildings b), building_dist AS (SELECT b.id, b.subtype, b.building_name, b.height, ST_Distance(b.geom_3763, p.geom_3763) AS distance_m FROM buildings b CROSS JOIN point p WHERE ST_Distance(b.geom_3763, p.geom_3763) <= 1000), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subtype ORDER BY height DESC, id) AS rn FROM building_dist), top3 AS (SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3) SELECT subtype, building_name, height, SUM(height) OVER (PARTITION BY subtype ORDER BY height DESC, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_height_m FROM top3 ORDER BY subtype, rn;
